newsitem.title: MEXICO: Bancomer sees Mexico '97 GDP growth at 4.8 pct.
newsitem.headline: Bancomer sees Mexico '97 GDP growth at 4.8 pct.

text.p: Mexico's second biggest banking group Bancomer Friday forecast Mexico's economic growth at 4.8 percent for 1997 and nearly five percent for next year.

In its monthly report Grupo Financiera Bancomer also predicted inflation at 1.0 percent a month at mid-year, but did not dismiss the possibility that seasonal factors among others might generate a rebound in inflation.
The group said its 4.8 percent growth forecast for gross domestic product was based on current economic indicators.
Earlier on Friday a central bank survey of 27 economic consultants showed average forecasts for 1997 GDP growth slipping 0.16 percent to 4.81 percent.
Price increases could reach an annualised 17.6 percent by December 1997, it added.
It said the next meeting of the U.S. Federal Reserve and Mexico's July elections could exert some influence on interest rates and the exchange rate.
"The short term perspectives are for some volatility in nominal interest rates and a high level of real rates...the ceiling for nominal rates will be around 24 percent," it said.
It saw the exchange rate maintaining its relative stability in nominal terms, and said it did not expect any sharp adjustments in its parity.
Bancomer predicted an orderly evolution of the exchange rate to 8.65 pesos to the dollar by end-1997.
It also said it could foresee the trade surplus diminishing more rapidly than it has to date.
If the economy adheres to its current stabilisation path, bank deposits would increase rapidly, it added.
The bank said worker productivity had increased at an annual average of 5.0 percent since 1987, creating a base for sustainable growth in real salaries.

Antonio Castro, director of independent economic consultancy CAPEM-Ciemex Wefa, said separately that Mexico GDP could grow at eight percent a year from just over five percent recorded last year if income and consumption taxes were reduced. ((--Mexico City newsroom +525 728 7905))
